artifact: exp59 Slice 5 -- Ray actor path vs HPX action path, plane-labeled juxtaposition
pipeline_note: QD8/QD32/QD128 pipeline rows exist on both sides (Ray object-refs + ray.get(list); HPX wait_all over futures) but are OUT OF SCOPE for this comparison -- different batching mechanisms, amortized makespan/N is not a latency.
plane_asymmetry_note: Ray numbers are observed in Python around ray.get (full actor RTT: Python frame + core-worker gRPC IPC + object-ref ownership/ray.get + cross-node transport + remote exec + result fetch). HPX numbers are caller-observed C++ hpx::async(...).get() RTT on the root locality (future suspend/resume + TCP parcel serialization + transport), NO Python boundary and NO object-ref ownership protocol. These are two different rulers, NOT two runtimes on one axis.
ray_plane_attribution_caveat: per-call steady-state floor is dominated by the Python boundary + core-worker IPC + object-ref/ray.get path; it is NOT cloudpickle (amortized by warmup) and NOT plasma (closed-int64 is inlined, not a plasma round-trip).
band_construction: per_island_median_of_per_island_percentiles_plus_min_max_spread (nearest-rank ceil(p*n)-1); pooled NOT used; identical on both sides
decision_rule: a gap inside the across-island jitter band is NOT a separable effect; the across-island min/max spread bounds what the per-island median can claim
placement_proof_basis_ray: hard NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(soft=False) + resolved Ray node_id + FQDN-normalized hostname (caller@nodeA != callee@nodeB), off_node_sample_count==0. Oracle correctness proves the intended actor executed and returned the expected closed-int64 result; the oracle value ALONE does not prove physical node placement.
placement_proof_basis_hpx: HPX locality id (here_locality != remote_locality) + same-node co-location (root/connector hostname == medusa00) for L1 / distinct localities for L2. Oracle correctness proves the intended locality executed and returned the expected closed-int64 result; the oracle value ALONE does not prove placement.
ray_cross_node_increment_note: ray_cross_node_p50 - ray_same_host_p50 = 741661 - 608695. WITHIN-RAY decomposition only. Same-host control is R=1 (indicative, not a band), so the increment is approximate; it shows most of the Ray QD1 floor (~609 us of ~742 us, ~82%) is present with NO network.
hpx_cross_node_increment_note: hpx_cross_node_p50 - hpx_same_node_p50 = 115831 - 76625. WITHIN-HPX decomposition only (both R=5 banded). Shows ~76.6 us of ~115.8 us (~66%) is local HPX stack + TCP-over-loopback software; only ~39 us is the eno16 wire. p99 wire increment ~83.8 us. loopback != zero cost; tcp_nodelay unverified -> Nagle held constant, not removed.
two_within_runtime_decompositions_never_: The Ray cross-node increment (~133 us) and the HPX wire increment (~39 us) are EACH within their own runtime and are NEVER subtracted or ratioed across runtimes. The shared finding is qualitative and per-runtime: in each runtime the QD1 floor is dominated by local stack, not network.
fairness_caveats: Ray plane = Python/Ray-actor-observed ray.get RTT; HPX plane = caller-observed C++ hpx::async(...).get() RTT. NOT the same measurement axis; no ratio/speedup is computable or reported.
Both sides per-island-primary R=5 bands with identical nearest-rank + median-of-medians construction; the Ray same-host control is R=1 (indicative only).
HPX is TCP-parcelport-specific (HPX's slowest parcelport); tcp_nodelay unverified -> Nagle/delayed-ACK is a possible QD1 confound held CONSTANT across L1/L2, not eliminated.
HPX kernel loopback (L1) is not zero-cost; the wire increment isolates only the physical leg above the loopback software path.
closed-int64 micro-workload; Rostam-allocation-specific; parity gated to medusa00/medusa01 and 10.42.5.
pipeline/QD8/QD32/QD128 are out of scope (different batching mechanisms); only QD1 is juxtaposed.
claim_fences: plane-labeled juxtaposition ONLY: no Ray-vs-HPX speedup, no ratio, no same-axis comparison, no 'HPX beats Ray'.
two within-runtime decompositions are reported per-runtime and are never crossed into a cross-runtime number.
no production / API / failure / restart / multi-node / general-fabric claim; no real inference.

Ray placement proven by hard NodeAffinity + Ray node_id + FQDN-normalized hostname; oracle correctness proves the intended actor executed and returned the expected closed-int64, NOT physical placement by itself.
HPX numbers are runtime-internal C++ caller RTT; they are NOT user-facing Python call-path numbers and are not on the Ray axis.
